title: Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong set to miss up to six weeks with hamstring injury
content:
Frenkie de Jong is facing up to six weeks on the sidelines for Barcelona after picking up a hamstring injury in training.

De Jong, 28, has made 31 appearances for the Catalan side this season, providing four assists in La Liga and scoring in Sunday’s win over Levante.

His absence comes after fellow midfielder Pedri returned from a second hamstring issue this season on the weekend, coming off the bench in the 66th minute. The match was also Raphinha’s first match back after the same injury had ruled him out of 13 games.

De Jong has captained Barcelona in seven of their previous eight league games. The midfielder also started in seven of the Netherlands’ eight World Cup qualifiers last year.

Barcelona’s win over Levante marked an end to a patch of poor performances that saw them lose 2-1 to ten-man Girona in the league and 4-0 to Atletico Madrid in the first leg of their Copa del Rey semi-final. Hansi Flick’s side remain top of La Liga, though, one point ahead of Real Madrid.

Despite their league place, Barcelona’s injuries have been a point of contention this season, with 12 players having picked up issues by November, which multiple dressing-room sources believe has contributed to their earlier dip in form.

Just when Flick was envisaging the return of his dream partnership in midfield, with Pedri coming back from injury last Saturday, Barca get hit with this De Jong news.

There is never good timing for an injury, but this feels particularly important given the stage of the season Barca are going through. Having De Jong sidelined for the next month would mean losing him for, at least, the first leg of the Champions League round of 16. Let alone the Copa del Rey semi-finals, where the Catalans are looking to stage an improbable comeback against Atletico.

De Jong is a fundamental piece in Flick’s plans with a special skill set nobody can replace: the press-resistance, physicality to cover a lot of ground and ability to break lines carrying the ball forward. But for those who chose to look at it with a more optimistic lens, Barca have Marc Bernal in that role.

This feels like a step-up moment for the 18-year-old, who is now going through his best moment of the season. He started his second La Liga game of the campaign last weekend and delivered an excellent performance, scoring the opener in Barca’s 3-0 win against Levante.

Bernal has been carefully managed this season, as he returned from an anterior cruciate ligament injury. Given his young age, Barca and Flick wanted to make sure he followed the right steps in the recovery process. Now, he is better than ever, and with De Jong out, you can expect to see his involvement increasing.

A big part of Barca’s hopes in the coming weeks will go through how well Bernal takes the increased minutes load, and whether Pedri keeps progressing adequately in his return from injury. Because this will probably become Flick’s new midfield partnership.
